pony.text: It eyes your pockets, then your face. It has decided there are no apples. It looks very let down.

pony_keeper.text: Dartmoor ponies roam free, but every one belongs to a farmer. Each autumn we round them up in a 'drift'.
It's a very old tradition. The ponies think it's a prank. We think it's hard work.

tor_walker.text: Tors are granite blocks, left standing when the softer rock around them wore away. Over millions of years, mind.
The moor has 160-odd of them. I'm on tor number 71 this year. I've started naming the rocks.

moor_birdwatcher.text: Dartmoor has skylarks, wheatears, cuckoos and the odd ring ouzel.
Keep your voice low. The ponies take offence at loud walkers. And the ouzels aren't impressed either.

stone_row_fan.text: Dartmoor has more Bronze Age remains than almost anywhere in Britain: stone rows, circles, hut circles, 3,500 years old.
I dug a hut circle on my first day. Then it rained, and we had to put the trench back. In fairness it was a good hut.

then.text: The hound has not come out for the brochure. Frankly I think it's being difficult. I've sent a polite email. To the moor.
Do cross the moor, please. Tintagel's the next stop on my itinerary. I'm told there's a cave.

else.text: Ah! A walker! Splendid. Do keep behind the cordon. The cordon is the grass.
Sir Rupert Ashcombe, Regional Director, England. We're surveying Hound Tor for the new brochure. 'The Hound of the Baskervilles Experience'. Hound included. Subject to availability.
Two Wardens crouch at the foot of the tor, one holding a net, the other a packet of mints. A Dartmoor pony watches them with open contempt.
Sir, the hound won't come out. We've tried the whistle. We've tried the mints. A pony ate the mints.
Then we need a bigger net. And a smaller pony.
The Wild Hunt rides across these tors, you know. Or something like it. A phantom hound, red eyes, a splendid night at the pub afterwards. It's a revenue stream, young person.

then.text: Not mine? My dear child, I have a deed. It's a rather good deed. It has a ribbon.
Still, I'm told you can battle. Not today. I'm rather busy being busy. I shall see you at Tintagel.

else.text: The brochure is in draft! It has a pull-out map and a competition. Win a night in a haunted tor. Terms apply. The terms are screaming.
I shall be at Tintagel presently. Do come by. I'll show you the cave. It's going to be a gift shop.

then.text: The oldest box on Dartmoor. You've stamped it, so you're one of us now. Mind the bog on the way down.
Cranmere Pool! You made it. Took me three goes and a sock full of bog. The box is in that cairn there, by the visitors' book.
You stamp your book: a little bottle with a card in it, and the date 1854.
That's the set. Go and tell the letterboxer on the B3212. Mind, she'll have another job for you. She always does.

else.text: Cranmere Pool, the first letterbox of them all. Find the two down by the Exe first, then come back up. It's tradition, and also I'm having my sandwiches.
